bullets.title: Carlos Ghosn: The Last Flight
bullets.note: ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jdfaO98M_XM), [Apple TV](https://tv.apple.com/us/movie/carlos-ghosn-the-last-flight/umc.cmc.1jkf496fskdrm4zqg0borq8f1?action=play)). From the description: “Carlos Ghosn, charged with financial crimes, stunned the world by fleeing Japan. This documentary sheds light on this complex and multilayered story and divulges new details on his spectacular escape.” You can watch the trailer [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rKftGmjdZ7w). I wasn’t initially excited about this, as I assumed it was a straightforward case of fraud. It turns out to be more like a Russian nesting doll of companies vs. companies, countries vs. countries, and a hyper-aggressive businessman (Ghosn) vs. the odds. It doesn’t paint him as a supervillain or as a simply misunderstood hero, and therein lies the nuance. I thoroughly enjoyed the unexpected twists of this doc, and the production value is outstanding. Carlos could make an interesting podcast guest at some point…

bullets.title: The Elliotts
bullets.note: on [_Heavyweight_](https://open.spotify.com/show/5c26B28vZMN8PG0Nppmn5G), hosted by [Jonathan Goldstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Goldstein_(author)) ([@J\_Goldstein](https://mobile.twitter.com/j_goldstein)). The description: “In 1525, the Archbishop of Glasgow placed a curse on the Elliott family. Now, 500 years later, one very unlucky branch of the Elliotts wants it lifted.” I found this incredibly entertaining and thought-provoking. Placebo effect or not, you’ll have a lot of laughs along the way.
